The `prism` filter lets a single Div, Span, CodeBlock, or Heading carry **conditional attributes**: each output format picks its own values from format-prefixed keys, so the same prose or code can be styled differently in HTML, revealjs, and Typst without duplication.

Attributes are keyed `format:name="value"`.
At render time, attributes whose `format` matches the active output are re-emitted as `name="value"`; the rest are dropped.
Unprefixed attributes pass through unchanged.

## How prefixes resolve

Prism matches each prefix against the **target format** of the current render, resolved from `quarto.format.format_identifier()["target-format"]`.
Matching is **exact**, so `html:` targets HTML output without affecting revealjs.

This document is rendered to three formats:

| Active format | Matching prefix |
| ------------- | --------------- |
| `html`        | `html:`         |
| `revealjs`    | `revealjs:`     |
| `typst`       | `typst:`        |

## Format-scoped attributes on Divs

Each prefix is independent: `html:style` is applied only under HTML, `revealjs:style` only under revealjs, and `typst:fill` only under Typst.
The unprefixed `note` attribute is preserved everywhere.

```markdown
::: {
  note="kept everywhere"
  html:style="color: hotpink;"
  revealjs:style="color: deepskyblue;"
  typst:fill='rgb("#b22222")'
}
This paragraph is pink in HTML, blue in revealjs, and unstyled in Typst.
:::
```

::: {
  note="kept everywhere"
  html:style="color: hotpink;"
  revealjs:style="color: deepskyblue;"
  typst:fill='rgb("#b22222")'
}
This paragraph is pink in HTML, blue in revealjs, and unstyled in Typst.
:::

## Override behaviour

A format-scoped attribute overrides a static attribute of the same name.
Under HTML the `html:` value wins; under revealjs the `revealjs:` value wins; under Typst no prefix matches, so the static `gray` is kept.

```markdown
::: {
  style="color: gray;"
  html:style="color: rebeccapurple;"
  revealjs:style="color: forestgreen;"
}
This paragraph reads as purple in HTML, green in revealjs, and gray in Typst.
:::
```

::: {
  style="color: gray;"
  html:style="color: rebeccapurple;"
  revealjs:style="color: forestgreen;"
}
This paragraph reads as purple in HTML, green in revealjs, and gray in Typst.
:::

## Format-scoped attributes on Spans

Inline content carries format-scoped attributes the same way.

```markdown
The next sentence styles a
[single span]{html:style="background: yellow; padding: 0 0.2em;" revealjs:style="background: lightyellow; padding: 0 0.2em;"}
only under the matching format.
```

The next sentence styles a [single span]{html:style="background: yellow; padding: 0 0.2em;" revealjs:style="background: lightyellow; padding: 0 0.2em;"} only under the matching format.

## Format-scoped attributes on CodeBlocks

CodeBlocks accept the same syntax.

````markdown
```{
  .r
  html:style="background: #f6f8fa; padding: 0.5em;"
  revealjs:style="background: #1f2937; color: #e5e7eb; padding: 0.5em;"
}
1 + 1
```
````

```{
  .r
  html:style="background: #f6f8fa; padding: 0.5em;"
  revealjs:style="background: #1f2937; color: #e5e7eb; padding: 0.5em;"
}
1 + 1
```

## Format-scoped attributes on headings

Headings carry format-scoped attributes through their `{...}` attribute block.

```markdown
### Styled heading {html:style="color: hotpink;" revealjs:style="color: deepskyblue;" typst:fill='rgb("#b22222")'}
```

### Styled heading {html:style="color: hotpink;" revealjs:style="color: deepskyblue;" typst:fill='rgb("#b22222")'}

## Unmatched prefixes are dropped

Prefixes that do not resolve to the active target format are removed entirely.
The next Div carries only `revealjs:` and `typst:` attributes; under HTML it therefore renders as plain content with no `style` attribute.

```markdown
::: {revealjs:style="color: indigo;" typst:fill='rgb("#0d9488")'}
Plain content in HTML; styled in revealjs and Typst.
:::
```

::: {revealjs:style="color: indigo;" typst:fill='rgb("#0d9488")'}
Plain content in HTML; styled in revealjs and Typst.
:::

## Format-group aliases

The `slide` alias matches every HTML slide format: `revealjs`, `slidy`, `s5`, `dzslides`, and `slideous`.
A single `slide:` prefix targets the whole group, so the next Div is styled under revealjs without naming each slide format.
Under HTML and Typst no slide format is active, so the `slide:` value is dropped.

```markdown
::: {slide:style="color: chocolate;"}
Styled under any HTML slide format; plain in HTML and Typst.
:::
```

::: {slide:style="color: chocolate;"}
Styled under any HTML slide format; plain in HTML and Typst.
:::

An exact format prefix wins over the `slide` alias for the same attribute name.
Under revealjs the `revealjs:` value applies; under any other slide format the `slide:` value would apply instead.

```markdown
::: {slide:style="color: teal;" revealjs:style="color: crimson;"}
Crimson under revealjs, teal under the other slide formats.
:::
```

::: {slide:style="color: teal;" revealjs:style="color: crimson;"}
Crimson under revealjs, teal under the other slide formats.
:::

## Default fallback

A `default:name` prefix provides a fallback value, applied only when no format-specific variant of the same name matched the active format.
Under HTML the `html:` value wins; under revealjs and Typst no specific variant matches, so the `default:` value is used.

```markdown
::: {default:style="color: gray;" html:style="color: rebeccapurple;"}
Purple under HTML, gray under revealjs and Typst.
:::
```

::: {default:style="color: gray;" html:style="color: rebeccapurple;"}
Purple under HTML, gray under revealjs and Typst.
:::

## Conflict between static, `default:`, and exact prefix

When the same attribute name carries a static unprefixed value, a `default:` fallback, and a format-scoped value, the higher-rank entry wins and the others are dropped from the output.
Under HTML the exact `html:` value wins; under revealjs and Typst no exact match exists, so the `default:` value wins; the static `gray` is never used because `default:` always outranks it.

```markdown
::: {style="color: gray;" default:style="color: silver;" html:style="color: crimson;"}
Crimson under HTML, silver under revealjs and Typst, never gray.
:::
```

::: {style="color: gray;" default:style="color: silver;" html:style="color: crimson;"}
Crimson under HTML, silver under revealjs and Typst, never gray.
:::

## Surface typos with `warn-on-drop`

Format-scoped attributes whose prefix does not match are silently dropped by default.
Set `extensions.prism.warn-on-drop: true` to emit a Quarto warning each time this happens, which makes typos in prefixes visible during render.

```yaml
extensions:
  prism:
    warn-on-drop: true
```

A typo such as `revaeljs:style="..."` then surfaces in the build log as `(W) [prism] Dropped attribute(s) 'revaeljs:style' on #mybox because no prefix matched target format 'revealjs'.`.
